newsitem.title: UK: UK seen able to absorb more hotel flotations.
newsitem.headline: UK seen able to absorb more hotel flotations.

text.p: Hotel flotations continue to crowd the London Stock Exchange, but despite some concerns that the market is reaching saturation analysts said on Friday the appetite for quality hotel companies has not yet been sated.

"It's a good business if you're in the right segment," said Jonathan Bodlender, chairman of the Horwarth consultant group. "It's a profitable business, and the institutions will always have an appetite for that."
No fewer than a half dozen hotel companies have gone public over the last six months, and more are following.
Thistle Hotels, Britain's second-largest hotel chain after Granada Group's Forte hotels, is scheduled to go public in October in a flotation designed to raise 250 million pounds ($388.8 million).
The group, whose 100 properties include London's Grosvenor and Royal Horseguards hotels, is expected to command a market value of 1.0 to 1.5 billion pounds.

Principal Hotels, a group of 21 provincial hotels throughout the UK, earlier this month announced plans to list on the London Stock Exchange and said it expects to have a market value of about 100 million pounds.
These flotations come on the heels of public offerings over recent months by Millennium & Copthorne, Jarvis Hotels, Macdonald Hotels and Cliveden Plc.
Lonrho Plc had announced plans to float its Metropole and Princess hotels, but recently said it was reconsidering because it had received bid interest.

Some analysts have said the move signalled concerns by Lonrho about its reception in the market. Others, however, said Lonrho's rethinking underscores the value of hotel companies and leaves that much more capacity to absorb other hotel flotations.
"The Princess, Metropole thing has been pulled, so that gives us a bit of spare capacity," said one analyst.

"I know of two or three purchasers in the UK who would give their eye teeth for the Metropole," said John Lewis, chairman of both Principal Hotels and Cliveden. Metropole is a UK-based chain of four-star hotels. Likewise, there is strong interest in the U.S. for the Princess hotels, Lonrho's five-star resort properties located in Acapulco, Mexico, and the Caribbean.

Lewis said Granada's acquisition of Forte last January has released funds for other hotel investments. The money raised by hotel flotations this year has yet to equal what was taken out by the Granada acquisition of Forte, he said.
And compared to other industries, the UK hotel sector still has relatively few publicly listed companies.

The continuing prosperity of the hotel industry underpins investment interest in the sector. In addition, the desire by financial institutions such as pension funds to invest in publicly quoted hotel companies is fuelling flotations.
"The institutions two or three years ago realised they were underinvested in a sector that was growing but the vehicles for them to invest weren't there," said Horwath's Bodlender.

Analysts said they do have doubts about the viability of floating smaller hotel companies such as Principal Hotels. "I think Principal will have trouble," said one analyst. "The only way you can sell it is by discounting to existing offers."

The drop in the share price of Jarvis Hotels below its June flotation price has been pointed to by some as weakness in the market for hotel companies. Jarvis on Friday was trading at 158 pence, compared to its flotation price of 175.

Others, however, note that the drop in Jarvis' shares reflected problems in how the flotation was handled. The company had listed a price range in its prospectus, but later priced the flotation above the published range.
"I think Jarvis was badly managed," said Lewis. "They jacked the price up at the last minute and upset the institutions."

Lewis said that Principal, like Cliveden, offers unique properties of classic, period hotels in key locations. Principal expects it room rate, currently at an average of 40.70 pounds, to rise at least 10 percent in 1997. Occupancy in 1996 is forecast at about 71 percent, he said.
